In SMILES, "Clc1ccc(N)cc1" means Cl attached to carbon 1, NH2 attached to carbon 4. Not same carbon. To have both on same carbon, you need "Clc1c(N)cccc1". That is 1-chloro-2-aminobenzene? Actually carbon 1 has Cl, carbon 2 has NH2. Not same.

Thus maybe template is for nitro attached to aromatic carbon that also has Cl (i.e., nitro-chlorobenzene). After reduction, you get aniline with Cl still attached to same carbon (i.e., chlorobenzene with NH2 substituent on same carbon? That's not possible). I'm confused.
